name: Proti
summary: One of the Princes’ Islands, associated with the death of Romanos IV after his deposition and blinding.
overview: Proti, now usually identified with Kinaliada in the Princes’ Islands, belonged to the island world near Constantinople used for exile and confinement.
Romanos IV Diogenes died there in 1072 after defeat, deposition, and blinding.

imageInfo.caption: One of the Princes’ Islands off Constantinople, a traditional place of Byzantine exile.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Princes’ Islands were close enough to Constantinople to serve imperial politics, exile, and monastic life. Proti appears in Byzantine political memory through the fate of Romanos IV.

contentSections.title: Medieval historical context
paragraphs: After Manzikert and civil conflict, Romanos IV was deposed and blinded. He died on Proti in 1072, showing the brutal consequences of Byzantine succession politics.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: The island’s significance in IronCodex comes from the end of a Byzantine emperor whose defeat at Manzikert became a turning point in Anatolian history.
